newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK EQUITIES CONTINUE TO DROP ON HIGHER RATES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK EQUITIES CONTINUE TO DROP ON HIGHER RATES.

text.p: Investors in Greek equities nursed large losses for the fourth day running, keeping a wary eye on spiking short drachma rates and continuing unrest in the forex market.
"Equities are suffering from the brief turmoil in the interbank market but the pressure should ease next week as liquidity has been restored," said George Athanasakis, anlyst at Alpha Securities.
The Athens general index fell back 1.24 percent or 19.37 points to 1,537.09 from Thursday's 1,556.46 close, easing at the last stages of trading from an intra-day low of 1,531.46.
Depos and forex forwards were firm but off their peaks on a liquidity squeeze linked to forex outflows on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The one-month Athibor, Greece's reference interbank rate, firmed another 36 basis points to 12.73 percent on Friday. It stood at 11.58 percent on Tuesday.
The central bank allocated nearly 100 billion drachmas in five-day repo at 12.90 percent to boost liquidity.
The drachma was stronger against the ecu and the dollar, fixed at 281.6 and 309.86, respectively, at the Bank of Greece's fixing on Friday.
"Investor confidence will be restored as soon as six-month results of banks are out showing impressive profit growth, both from pure banking operations and portfolio trading," said Athanasakis.
Buying should be selective at current price levels in banks and industrial blue chips which will susprise the market with the capacity to accelerate their profitability, he added.
Despite the money market-led selling pressure, equities were not seen overvalued and selective buying was recommended.

"The broader market remains reasonably priced at a 14.5 P/E multiple based on post-tax 1997 earnings as compared to an equivalent valuation of 12.5 for 12-month government paper," Alpha's Athanasakis said.
Turnover was boosted to 22.8 billion drachmas on volume of 4.9 million shares by sizeable block trades of shares placed with foreign and local institutional investors.

A total of 1.33 million shares of Lavipharm were placed at 2,500 drachmas by Sigma Securities and 0.4 million shares of Sidenor SID.AT at 13,000 drachmas by NIBID through National Securities, Alpha Brokerage, Telesis Securities and Hermes Securities.
Declining stocks beat advancers 144 to 55 with 29 shares unchanged on 228 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.4-$10.7. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,110-1,140 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,023-1,083 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock settled 50 drachmas lower at at 6,145.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 594.63-632.59 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $66.84-$69.56. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,065-3,279 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.07 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 211-242 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ****
